This is not measuring a gap to the rear of a leading vehicle, and it does not turn a familiar road into a visible one. Starting only when you reach the marker does not measure the same interval. The following check uses the vehicle ahead passing a marker to consider the separation behind it. Both involve counting, but changing the reference changes what is being measured. A good result in one does not automatically establish the other. The source’s sight-distance and following checks offer different ways to consider part of that room. Retain their references and respond to the result rather than use the count as a guarantee that nothing can change. A gap can shrink, the visible view can shorten and conditions can become less favorable.
